M LAW / PROPOSED OPERATING MODEL
Presenter guide ↗Open onboarding ↗

More time for clients.
A clear owner for every action.

A proposed division of work for a midsize New York personal injury firm. Product examples below are a researched planning assumption. M Law's current products, seat counts, prices and contracts have not been confirmed.

The proposition to Adnan

“Your team stays responsible for the legal work and the client relationship. The agents collect information, organize the file, chase routine next steps and prepare work for review. We retire a subscription only after its replacement proves the complete workflow.”

Current state: working prototype. One connected local drafting agent has completed a matter-based request. Intake, booking, task, draft and review workflows work in the demonstration. The full agent team below is a target operating model, not a claim that every worker is deployed.

What each person does

PersonOwns the work and decisionsWhat the agents take off the desk
Adnan / managing partnerCase acceptance and conflict resolution; litigation strategy; supervising attorneys; significant negotiations; client advice and settlement recommendations; firm policies, access and final go-live decisions.A daily exception brief, intake summaries, draft recommendations, missing-evidence alerts, workload visibility and work awaiting a decision.
Junior attorneysInterview clients and witnesses; investigate; verify facts and authorities; develop arguments; review/edit drafts; advise clients; negotiate within authority; conduct depositions and appearances; verify deadlines and filing requirements.First drafts, chronologies, record comparisons, research candidates, exhibit indexes, draft discovery, missing-document lists and next-step queues.
Paralegals / case managersValidate received records and source matching; obtain authorizations; resolve missing or inconsistent information; coordinate providers; manage discovery logistics; prepare filing packages under attorney supervision.Document classification, extraction, routine request preparation, follow-up schedules, provider/bill tracking, task creation and status summaries.
Office / intake teamTake escalated or sensitive calls; resolve scheduling exceptions; confirm identity and contact details; handle physical mail; correct duplicates; help clients who need a person; monitor missed contacts.Routine 24/7 intake, approved FAQs, consultation reservations, callback capture, approved reminders and verified status delivery.
Bookkeeper / accountantVerify expenses and liens; reconcile bank and client ledgers; approve accounting treatment; run payroll/tax work; review settlement statements and authorized disbursements.Expense extraction, draft allocations, discrepancy flags, reconciliation suggestions and management reporting.
Named system ownerMaintain hosting, updates, access, backups, recovery, monitoring and incident response. This role can be an accountable staff member or retained technical provider.Health checks, backup execution, failure alerts, audit exports and routine maintenance reports once deployed.

Attorneys do substantive legal work; they are not merely approval buttons. Clients retain decisions that require their authorization, including settlement. Staffing changes should follow measured workload and service results, not a forecast that every call or exception will disappear.

What the system may do automatically

Within a firm-approved policy

Save intake details, classify incoming items, propose tasks, reserve permitted calendar slots, run backups and send preapproved administrative reminders after identity, consent and delivery controls are in place.

Exceptions go to a named person: emergency language, uncertain identity, conflicts, complaints, missing authority, low confidence, contradictory sources or a failed external action.

Requires human judgment or authorization

Representation and conflict decisions, legal advice and strategy, verified deadlines, substantive client communications, demands, court submissions, settlement recommendations, waivers and money movement.

New York's AI rules preserve attorneys' responsibility for court submissions. Our design keeps factual and legal verification with the attorney. New York Courts, Part 161 ↗

A practical retirement sequence

  1. Inventory: product, purpose, paid seats, actual monthly/annual cost, renewal/cancellation dates, contract term, export owner and every dependency.
  2. Pilot one narrow workflow: intake, callbacks and internal consultation booking are the first proposal. Agree success measures with Adnan before testing.
  3. Prove the replacement: use representative routine and exception cases. Compare records and outcomes; test restore, outage handling and human escalation.
  4. Run in parallel: retain the current system until users and the responsible attorney accept the replacement. Determine the duration from actual volume and risk.
  5. Export, reconcile and sign off: check counts and attachments, preserve required records, resolve failures, document owner approval, then cancel according to the contract.

Net saving = subscriptions actually retired − hosting − model/voice usage or hardware − phone/email delivery − backup/security − maintenance/support. No savings total is credible until actual invoices and usage are known.

Five questions to ask Adnan

  1. What do you use for matters, intake, files, email, phones, research, accounting and signatures—and who owns each account?
  2. Which repetitive work creates the most delay or rework?
  3. Which decisions must come to you, and which can junior attorneys or office staff own?
  4. Who handles after-hours escalation, identity problems and upset clients?
  5. Which one workflow and one team member should be the first pilot?

Record the answers in Launch plan and Software inventory, then download the meeting brief.
